transcript:
[Header]
Date: 2027-03-08
Start: 10:00 PST
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Priya, Marcus, Samir, Alicia, Evan, Lena, Noah

Summary: Quick workshop to align IT and FinOps on identity provisioning, seat/license reconciliation, and short-lived service accounts. Focus on runbook updates, audit artifacts for SOC2, and immediate queries for license consumption.

Topics: Provisioning runbook, SSO/SAML edge cases, KMS key access patterns, license seat counts, service account lifecycle, audit logging retention.

[00:00] Priya: Alright, hi everyone, thanks for making time. I think we have, what, forty five minutes-ish. The goal is, um, align on the provisioning runbook changes and get the license numbers we need for finance.

[01:12] Marcus: Yep, from finance side we just need a clean per-month seat consumption and any volume spikes. The last report had duplicates from service accounts that were counted as seats, so we need to separate those.

[02:30] Alicia: Right — and on the IT side we've been seeing a few manual onboardings. We want to push to automated SAML groups, but there's edge cases — contractors and cross-org collaborators don't always map cleanly.

[04:05] Samir: Quick note: for SOC2 we'll need proof of provisioning flows — screenshots aren't enough, we need logs, timestamps, and the RBAC policy references. Also need to show deprovisioning within X days for leavers.

[06:20] Lena: Yeah, and audit logs need to be centrally retained. What's our current log retention for SSO events? I thought it was 90 days but not sure.

[07:10] Priya: It's 90 on Splunk but long-term archive is cold storage for 365 days. We should include the retention SLAs in the runbook doc.

[09:00] Noah: About service accounts — a lot of older infra uses long-lived keys. We need a migration plan to short-lived tokens, maybe use KMS-bound keywraps or cloud provider STS.

[11:45] Marcus: Will that affect billing? If we create ephemeral machines that rotate identities more often, do we get hit with more API calls that change cost profiles?

[12:30] Samir: Good question. Typically token rotation itself is tiny cost — the bigger cost is staff time and engineering cycles. But if we move to a managed identity provider, there might be license seats for machine identities — we need to check.

[14:50] Alicia: On the SAML groups: contractors should map to a "contractor" group with limited access and auto-expire — we can set group membership TTL via SCIM provisioning if the IDP supports it.

[16:05] Priya: Ok, can we document the SCIM mapping examples? I'm thinking include snippet: group -> role mapping, default access, and exception approval flow.

[18:30] Samir: I'll paste the example SCIM payload later, but FYI auto-provisioning sometimes mungs emails with nonstandard domains, so we need canonicalization steps.

[20:00] Lena: Also for SOC2 control CC-4 we need an owner for each provisioning exception. The runbook should list owners and sign-off paths.

[22:15] Noah: For the seat count cleanup — we need a rule to exclude service accounts. Maybe mark accounts with 'service:' prefix and filter them out of seat reports.

[24:40] Marcus: We can add a filter in the billing pipeline — but historically service accounts were created without consistent naming. I'll run a query that looks for non-human patterns and return candidates.

[26:10] Alicia: Can we add a manual review step? Marcus runs the filter, then we get a list and IT reviews to confirm which are service accounts vs contractors.

[28:00] Priya: Sounds good. Also, timeline: Marcus can deliver initial CSV by Wednesday. Samir, you said you'd prototype ephemeral service account pattern — can you target next Tuesday?

[30:20] Samir: Yes, I'll spin up a PoC using short-lived signed JWTs and a key-rotation hook. It'll show the lifecycle and logs.

[32:10] Lena: For compliance evidence, we need the log queries and the retention snapshot. Can you capture a saved query in Splunk and export the sample within the evidence binder?

[34:05] Priya: I'll create the evidence folder in Confluence and add the runbook draft. We'll include links to the saved queries and the SCIM mapping snippet.

[36:25] Evan: On FinOps, if we change seat definitions, we need to send a note to procurement because license seats are contractually defined. We might need an amendment.

[38:00] Marcus: Understood. I'll draft a short email for procurement once we have the cleaned dataset. Also checking whether vendor billing supports prorated adjustments.

[40:15] Priya: Any blockers on SSO providers? We currently use Okta; we've evaluated OneLogin for a couple teams but nothing committed.

[41:00] Samir: Okta supports SCIM group TTL with lifecycle events. Just check the SCIM schema mapping. I had one glitch where Okta sent group name as displayName and our parser expected 'name' — small mismatch.

[42:40] Alicia: We'll include the mapping table in the runbook. Also, document the fallback manual flow when SCIM errors occur.

[44:10] Priya: Great. Quick recap: Priya will update runbook and create Confluence folder; Marcus will run license extraction and share CSV; Samir will prototype ephemeral service accounts; Lena will validate SOC2 evidence; Alicia will assist with SCIM mapping and manual review. All aim to have first artifacts next week.

[46:00] Marcus: I'll share the initial CSV by 2027-03-10 EOD.

[46:30] Priya: Thanks everyone. I'll send calendar invite for the follow-up and include action items. Meeting adjourned.

[End]
